Fantastic! White wins material decisively:
- Bxd4 wins the knight (+3)
- After Re1+, Nxe1 wins the rook (+5)
- Net material gain is overwhelming

This is the key move: **Bxd4** is a fork/double attack pattern—the bishop on e5 attacks both the knight on d4 and potentially sets up tactics. More precisely, by capturing the knight, White eliminates Black's counterplay and after the forced Re1+ check, White's knight recaptures with a winning position.

**Coaching note (under 80 words):**
Look for undefended pieces! The Black knight on d4 was hanging (attacked by your bishop, nothing defending it). When you capture undefended pieces, always check if your opponent has forcing moves like checks. Here, Black's Re1+ doesn't save the game—your knight simply takes the rook on e1. You win first a knight, then a rook. Always capture hanging material, but make sure to calculate opponent checks one move deep.
